proposal.reactor_type: Tubular PFA coil reactor (single-stage, no photochemistry)
proposal.residence_time_basis: Total volumetric flow at reactor inlet (both liquid streams combined = 1.0 mL/min); reactor volume 8.0 mL gives 8 min residence time.
proposal.light_setup: None — thermal nitration, no photochemistry required.

streams.solvent: Concentrated sulfuric acid (H2SO4, 96–98 wt%) — the industrial batch solvent for mixed-acid nitration; substrate dissolved at 0.5 M

streams.contents: Mixed acid: fuming/concentrated HNO3 (≥90 wt%) pre-diluted in H2SO4 to give 2.5 M HNO3 in H2SO4

proposal.mixer_type: T-mixer or cross-mixer (PEEK or Hastelloy C-276, 0.5 mm bore) with active cooling jacket on mixer body
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Substrate in H2SO4 (S1) meets nitrating mixed acid (S2) at the T-mixer. This order mirrors the industrial practice of adding the substrate to the acid rather than acid to substrate, minimising local excess of nitronium ion and controlling exotherm. The mixer body is cooled to ≤10 °C to quench the initial mixing exotherm before the combined stream enters the heated reactor coil at 60 °C. Molar ratio HNO3:substrate = 2.5:1 to drive double nitration to completion (consistent with 89% dinitration yield in batch).
pre_reactor_steps: Substrate dissolution: dissolve aniline derivative in concentrated H2SO4 at room temperature with stirring; degas and load into syringe/reservoir for Pump A.

Mixed-acid preparation: carefully add fuming HNO3 to cold H2SO4 (ice bath, <10 °C, slow addition) to reach 2.5 M HNO3; cool to room temperature before loading into Pump B reservoir. CAUTION: highly exothermic — perform in fume hood with face shield.
System priming: prime both pumps with respective solutions, purge air, confirm stable flow rates before heating reactor.
Mixer cooling: circulate ice-water or chilled ethylene glycol/water through mixer jacket; confirm mixer outlet temperature ≤15 °C before starting reaction.
post_reactor_steps: BPR (back-pressure regulator, 7 bar): maintains liquid phase throughout; prevents boiling of H2SO4 mixture and suppresses any dissolved NOx gas evolution.

Inline quench stream (optional, recommended): a third pump (Pump C) delivers ice-cold water at 0.5 mL/min into a second T-mixer immediately after the BPR to dilute and quench the reaction; this is strongly advised for safety.
Collection vessel: product stream collected into a pre-cooled vessel containing ice and NaHCO3 solution for neutralisation.
Workup: neutralise carefully (exothermic), extract dinitrated product with ethyl acetate or dichloromethane, wash, dry, concentrate.
Analytics: HPLC or GC-MS to confirm dinitration regiochemistry and yield; Karl Fischer titration of water content if needed.
proposal.chemistry_notes: Nitration of aniline derivatives with mixed acid (HNO3/H2SO4) proceeds via electrophilic aromatic substitution (EAS) through the nitronium ion (NO2+) generated in situ. The amine group is a strong ortho/para director; double nitration at 60 °C with 2.5 equiv HNO3 is consistent with literature for activated substrates. Concentrated H2SO4 serves as both solvent and proton source to generate NO2+. Flow chemistry advantages: (1) precise temperature control eliminates hot-spots that cause over-nitration or oxidative degradation; (2) small reactor volume (8 mL) drastically reduces inventory of energetic mixed acid; (3) residence time of 8 min vs 4 h batch — acceleration factor ~30× due to improved mass/heat transfer and elimination of heat-up/cool-down time; (4) continuous BPR prevents gas evolution. Assumption: the 'industrial batch solvent' is H2SO4 (standard for mixed-acid nitration). If the actual substrate differs, HNO3 equivalents and temperature may need adjustment.

stage_parameters.purpose: Controlled mixing of substrate and nitrating agent; quench initial exotherm

stage_parameters.description: Reaction coil (PFA, 8 mL, 60 °C oil bath or heated block)
Post-BPR quench T-mixer (optional Pump C, ice-cold water)
stage_parameters.purpose: Dilution and thermal quench; stops reaction and reduces corrosivity before collection

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Batch: 4 h at 60 °C. Flow reactors achieve dramatically faster mass/heat transfer. Literature analogies for aromatic nitration in flow show 5–15 min residence times at equivalent temperatures. 8 min chosen conservatively to ensure complete double nitration while staying within safe thermal envelope. Can be optimised by DoE.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Total flow 1.0 mL/min (0.5 + 0.5 mL/min). Chosen to give 8 min residence in 8 mL reactor. Low enough for standard HPLC/syringe pumps; high enough for good mixing Reynolds number in 1 mm ID tubing (Re ≈ 20–50, laminar but adequate for reactive system).
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Matches batch protocol (60 °C). Flow control allows safe operation at this temperature with minimal risk of runaway due to small thermal mass.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Substrate at 0.5 M in combined stream (1.0 M in S1, diluted 1:1 at mixer). Practical for solubility in H2SO4 and for pump handling. HNO3 at 1.25 M in combined stream (2.5 M in S2, diluted 1:1), giving 2.5 equiv relative to substrate.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 7 bar (≈100 psi). Boiling point of H2SO4 mixtures is well above 60 °C, but BPR ensures no gas slugs from dissolved NOx (NO, NO2 can form as by-products). 7 bar is standard for liquid-phase flow nitration; compatible with PFA tubing rated >20 bar at 60 °C.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Simple tubular coil preferred over microreactor chip for corrosive mixed acid. PFA is chemically resistant to HNO3/H2SO4 at 60 °C. Coil format allows easy volume scaling.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA: excellent resistance to concentrated H2SO4 and HNO3 at 60 °C. PTFE is alternative but PFA is more transparent for visual inspection. Stainless steel and PEEK are NOT suitable for concentrated HNO3.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID: standard for lab-scale flow chemistry; gives reactor volume of 8 mL at ~3.2 m coil length (V = π×(0.5mm)²×L). Manageable coil size.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 8.0 mL = 1.0 mL/min × 8 min. Consistent with flow rate and residence time.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar_rationale: Prevents phase separation and gas evolution; standard practice for nitration flow systems.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: T-mixer or cross-mixer in PEEK or Hastelloy C-276 (both resistant to mixed acid). Bore 0.5 mm for good mixing. Cooling jacket critical to manage exotherm at point of mixing.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: Not applicable — purely thermal EAS nitration.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M_assumption: Substrate solubility in concentrated H2SO4 assumed adequate at 1.0 M; verify experimentally. If solubility is limiting, reduce to 0.25 M and adjust flow rates accordingly.

literature_analogies: Ducry, L.; Roberge, D. M. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2005, 44, 7972–7975 — adiabatic microreactor nitration of toluene; residence times 1–10 min at 50–80 °C.
Antes, J. et al. Chem. Eng. J. 2003, 101, 175–185 — nitration of aromatic compounds in microreactors with mixed acid; improved selectivity vs batch.
Roberge, D. M. et al. Org. Process Res. Dev. 2008, 12, 905–910 — industrial flow nitration; residence times 5–15 min, temperatures 40–80 °C.
Gutmann, B. et al. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2015, 54, 7219–7222 — continuous flow nitration review; safety and selectivity advantages.
Kockmann, N. et al. Chem. Eng. J. 2008, 135S, S110–S116 — mixing and reaction in microchannels for nitration; exotherm management.
safety_flags: CRITICAL — Mixed acid (HNO3/H2SO4): highly corrosive, strong oxidiser. All handling in fume hood with full PPE (face shield, acid-resistant gloves, lab coat). Emergency eyewash and shower nearby.

CRITICAL — Exothermic mixing: mixing of substrate with mixed acid is strongly exothermic. Mixer cooling to ≤10 °C is mandatory. Monitor mixer outlet temperature with inline thermocouple; install automatic pump shutoff if T > 30 °C at mixer outlet.

HIGH — Energetic intermediates/products: dinitroaniline derivatives are energetically sensitive. Avoid shock, friction, and heating of dry product. Characterise thermal stability (DSC) before scale-up.

HIGH — NOx gas evolution: nitrogen oxides (NO, NO2) may form as by-products. BPR maintains pressure to suppress gas evolution in reactor. Vent collection vessel to scrubber (NaOH solution). Work in fume hood.
HIGH — Pressure: system operates at 7 bar. Use pressure-rated PFA tubing and fittings (verify manufacturer ratings). Install pressure relief valve upstream of BPR rated at 15 bar.
MEDIUM — Pump compatibility: verify pump heads and seals are compatible with concentrated H2SO4 and HNO3. PTFE-lined syringe pumps or HPLC pumps with PTFE/ceramic heads recommended.
MEDIUM — Spill containment: place entire flow system in secondary containment tray (acid-resistant polypropylene). Have sodium bicarbonate and dry sand available for spill neutralisation.
MEDIUM — Scale-up caution: 8 mL reactor inventory is low (key safety advantage of flow). Do not scale by increasing concentration before thermal stability data are available; prefer numbering-up.

LOW — Substrate identity: exact aniline derivative not specified in protocol. Regiochemistry, solubility, and optimal HNO3 equivalents depend on substituents. Validate with small-scale experiments before full run.

ASSUMPTION — Solvent identity: 'industrial batch solvent' interpreted as concentrated H2SO4 (standard for mixed-acid nitration). If a different solvent was used (e.g., acetic acid, acetic anhydride), redesign required.
